title: The Return of the Contradiction
text: “Anyway, we managed to get through it somehow.”
“It was a piece of cake! If it weren’t for those meddling guys, I think it would’ve been even easier.”
“Yeah. Sakura thinks so too.”
Keel, Sakura-chan, Yuki-chan, and Kou all nodded in agreement. That’s right. I’d say this was a huge success.
“Well, well, this is still just the beginning… According to Motoyasu, the waves are only going to get tougher from here on out, right? So don’t let your guard down.”
Just as we were talking like this, the Captain of the Knight Order, who had gone over to Ren and Itsuki, declared in a loud voice.
“Well done, heroes! The King says a feast has been prepared for the party of heroes who overcame this wave. He’ll also be giving you a reward, so please come.”

Considering what’s in store for the future—and the fact that he’s only inviting us to harass my Father—he sure has the nerve to say that. Still, I suppose we should take what we’re offered. It’ll probably just be a severance payment, but 500 silver coins isn’t something to sneeze at. Well, given the money and equipment we can get in Siltvelt, it’s actually kind of extra cash. Since some weapon enhancements require direct payment, it certainly won’t hurt to have it.
“The diversion went well, but the real thing… I wonder if it’ll be tonight? Still, since Motoyasu-kun is on our side, I hope nothing happens…”

My father mutters to me, seemingly unable to fully hide his anxiety. That’s true. It’d be best if nothing happened, but given that we’re dealing with Trash and Crimson Swine, the possibility that they’ll pull something isn’t zero.

However, if we forcefully thwart their plans, it’ll change the course of events. But hey, Father’s level should be way higher now than it was in the first world. He won’t go down from just a little trouble. And besides, since I’m right here with him, I won’t let them have their way.
“Uh, excuse me…”
The villagers from Riyute Village who had taken refuge with us spoke up.
“What? Do you need something from us?”
Father replied in a friendly tone.
“Thank you so much. If it weren’t for you, I think everyone would have been in danger.”
“Y-you’re welcome. Are there any injuries? If you need anything, I can give you some of my leftover medicine.”
“We’re fine. There were no casualties… and the village made it through unscathed. It’s all thanks to the Shield Hero and the Spear Hero and their party.”
“R-really? I’m glad to hear that. Rebuilding will be tough, but hang in there, okay?”
“Yes, thank you so much!”

The villagers bowed deeply and seemed to head back to their homes. Their expressions spoke volumes of relief. While there was no major damage, a few buildings did sustain some damage from the monsters. …I think the damage is less severe than what Future Riyute Village suffered.

In any case, we managed to defend the village with minimal damage. Father’s achievements really are remarkable. Back then, he and Big Sister were the only two defending the village. Considering that it took all of us—including me—to finally hold the line, and yet the two of them managed to limit the damage to that extent, you can really see how skilled he is.
“Well then, let’s head back to the castle. I hear there’s a feast tonight, so everyone’s looking forward to it.”
“Yay! Feast time!”
“I can’t wait for Sakura!”
“You all are so crude.”
“Aren’t you looking forward to it, Yuki? I wonder if someone like Keel-kun—who’s about to drool any second—will show up.”
“I told you I’m not food! It’d be scary if he actually showed up!”
“Boo…”
Come to think of it, there was also that Lazy Pig. I wonder where he was and what he was doing. Surely he wasn’t slacking off even during the battle, was he? If he was, I’ll kick his butt.
“Yeah, Elena’s evacuation guidance was really efficient.”
“Booh…”
“Her instructions were spot-on, I must say.”
“But Elena-nee didn’t fight at all, though.”
Hmm, is that so? Well, I suppose there’s nothing to be done about it. Since my Father says so, I suppose I’ll raise my opinion of her just a little.
With such thoughts in mind, I followed the retreating knight corps. With a hint of unease, my Father and I followed behind them.
“Wow! Just as you’d expect from a Hero. I can’t hide my surprise—it’s a world of difference from the damage last time!”

Once night fell, Trash made a bold declaration in the castle’s banquet hall, and the feast began. “The damage from last time,” he said. I’ve only heard about it secondhand from Keel, Big Sister, and the village slaves, but apparently there were quite a few casualties.

Incidentally, thanks to Father and my efforts, the number of casualties this time was practically zero. Well, Father figured that if he declared our contributions here, it would just be brushed off, so he asked me to keep quiet.

Father’s reasoning was that if he’d known the reason from the start, he wouldn’t have been so frustrated. That’s typical of him. The only reason I’m here is to save on food costs and get some silver coins.
“Whoa! Let’s dig in!”

Keel and the others rush over to the buffet-style spread, piling food onto their plates and devouring it in big bites. What an appetite they have. It rivals even Filolial-sama during her growth spurt.
“Everyone sure eats a lot, huh?”
“It’s not as good as my brother’s cooking, though. You should cook tomorrow, big bro.”
“Yeah, yeah.”
“Sakura, too—”
“Kou, too… I want to pour this sauce on Keel-kun and lick it off.”
“How much more of me do you plan to eat before you’re satisfied?! I’m definitely not going to lose!”
Keel barks “Woof, woof” at Kou. Kou has already drizzled sauce on Keel and is licking his lips.
“Hey, hey, Kou, please stop going after Keel-kun.”
“Okay. Then if Keel-kun multiplies, give me one.”
“No… even if he multiplies, you’re not allowed to eat him…”
“What do you mean, ‘multiply me’?! What are you planning to do?!”
It’s such a heartwarming sight. Just watching them makes me happy. Seeing my Father taking care of Keel, Yuki-chan, and Kou really cleanses the soul.
Sakura-chan has joined the group and is enjoying her meal as well. Though, the folks around us are giving us dirty looks. Seriously… do they even know who did the most work here?

Well… while this carefree time is passing, chronologically speaking, we’re approaching the point where I was tricked by Crimson Swine and Trash and confronted my Father. Suddenly, Itsuki, looking rather displeased, starts walking toward us.
Seriously… if I don’t do it, Itsuki will. What should I do? I can’t just stay silent, so I guess I’ll step forward.
“Itsuki, what’s the matter?”
“Step aside. I need to speak with Naofumi-san.”
“So, what’s this about? I’ll handle it.”
“Motoyasu-san, I can’t talk to you!”

He tries to force me aside, but with a strength like Itsuki’s, it’s impossible for him to move me. My Father rushes over toward me, wondering what’s going on. Then, upon seeing Itsuki’s expression, he nods as if he understands everything.
“What’s going on?”
“It’s not ‘what’s going on’!”
Itsuki pointed at my Father.
“I heard it! Naofumi-san… no, Naofumi! That the people you called your ‘comrades’ are actually slaves!”
“…Well, that’s true.”

At the sound of Itsuki’s voice, Keel, Sakura-chan, Yuki-chan, and Kou all looked over at us. As for the Lazy Pig… he seems to be blending into the crowd, pretending to be an outsider and acting like none of this concerns him. And my father gave Itsuki a theatrical look, as if to say, “What on earth are you talking about?” Since we’d discussed the possibility of this happening beforehand, he didn’t seem all that surprised.
“So… what?”
“You admitted it!”
With an expression brimming with conviction, as if to say “Victory is mine,” Itsuki declared. In stark contrast to Itsuki, my father spoke with a look of exasperation.
“To be precise, Keel and Elena are slaves, and Sakura, Yuki, and Kou are monsters, right? So what?”
“Wha… Why are you saying that as if it’s perfectly normal?!”
“Did I say something strange? Well, it doesn’t sound good to others, but it doesn’t violate this country’s laws. In order to operate in this country—”
Before my father-in-law could finish his reply, Itsuki cut in, speaking rapidly.

“Enslaving people and forcing them onto a battlefield where they don’t even want to fight, making them engage in a life-and-death struggle—that’s not something a hero should even be accused of! Free them right now! Otherwise, I won’t forgive you.”
“What are you talking about! We’re fighting alongside my brother because we want to!”
At Itsuki’s words, Keel stepped in to counter. However, Itsuki didn’t seem willing to listen.
“I know you’re only saying that because you’re being controlled by a ‘slave mark’ that forces you to act as if you’re about to die. Don’t worry. I’ll save you all.”

“Ugh… I was wondering what you were going to say—that a hero shouldn’t use slaves? In this country, Demi-Humans aren’t recognized as anything other than slaves. Itsuki is glaring at his father-in-law, who has replied, as if he isn’t even hearing it. Crimson Swine and Trash approach with smirks on their faces. They’ve probably whispered something unnecessary to Itsuki.
“Even this guy, Keel—I took him in after the people of this country forcibly turned him into a slave.”
“That’s right! The people of this country slaughtered all the adults who were trying to rebuild the nation, and took away all the women and children who couldn’t fight!”

What Keel says is true. But Itsuki doesn’t change his expression at all—perhaps he believes the story he first heard from Crimson Swine and Trash. He’s probably convinced they’re being forced to say these things. Just like I used to be.
“Itsuki, this is a different world. When in Rome, do as the Romans do—the existence of slaves is simply unavoidable.”
“Unavoidable, you say? No, it’s not unavoidable at all! Naofumi! You’re wrong!”

“You’re right. I am wrong. I won’t deny that. In a normal Japan, what you’re saying, Itsuki, would be absolutely correct. But you shouldn’t assume that just because something is right, it’ll always be accepted. There are plenty of people who wouldn’t even make it to tomorrow if they didn’t do things that aren’t right.”
Even though my father said that, Itsuki’s expression seems to say he won’t budge an inch. My father’s words really strike a chord.

I did something utterly unforgivable during the Spirit Tortoise incident. I was condemned by the people as a natural consequence, but I’m still alive here today. Likewise, Ren and Itsuki from the first world must have faced the same fate as I did. Yet Father forgave us after just a mild scolding.

To put it bluntly, that isn’t the right thing to do. After all, we were the ones responsible for sacrificing so many people. But Father kept us alive because he needed the power of the hero within us.

And this is despite the fact that we cornered my Father time and time again, just as Itsuki is doing now. Yes, I suppose the world doesn’t run on righteousness alone. It contradicts the promise I made to Filo-tan a bit, but saving many people isn’t possible with just nice words. My Father taught me that important lesson through his actions.
“I’ve heard what Lord Itsuki had to say!”
That Trash declared, putting on a serious expression. The Trash pushed through the crowd and strode in with great fanfare.

He has some nerve saying that, considering he set Itsuki up from the very beginning. He sure is clever when it comes to harassment, isn’t he? Should I just kill him right now? No, that would drastically change the future.
“Then how about this? What if two heroes fight, and the winner’s claim is deemed correct?”
